---
title: "How to Use Voice Mode in ChatGPT on Your Phone (Step by Step)"
subtitle: "Turn your phone into a hands-free assistant with ChatGPT's voice mode — here's how to start today"
category: "how-to"
audience: "personal"
read_time_minutes: 6
tags: ["voice-ai", "chatgpt", "mobile", "getting-started"]
---

> **In short:** ChatGPT's voice mode lets you talk to the AI instead of typing, and it talks back out loud. You tap the waveform icon in the app, allow microphone access, and pick a voice. Basic voice is free; the more natural-sounding "Advanced Voice" needs a paid Plus plan.

Voice mode turns your phone into a hands-free helper. You can ask for a recipe step while your hands are covered in flour, or get a quick weather check while you're getting the kids in the car. The standard voice is built into the free app. A more natural-sounding "Advanced Voice" sits behind the paid plan.

Here's exactly how to set it up and start using it today.

---

## What you'll need before you start

Before Step 1, make sure these are in place:

- **The ChatGPT app** on iOS or Android (free download from the App Store or Google Play). Update it to the latest version if it's been a while.
- **A ChatGPT account** — a free account works for basic voice. The more natural-sounding **Advanced Voice Mode** needs a **Plus subscription** (around $20 USD/month).
- **Microphone permission** — your phone will ask, but it's worth checking in advance under your phone's privacy settings.
- **A reasonably quiet spot** for your first try, so the AI hears you clearly.

---

## Step 1 — Open the app and sign in

If you don't already have the ChatGPT app, download it from the App Store (iPhone) or Google Play (Android). Open it and sign in with your email, Google, or Apple ID. If you're new, tap **Sign up** and follow the prompts.

You'll land on the main chat screen. At the top, you'll see your profile icon (a circle with your initials or picture). Tap it once when you're ready to change settings.

> 💬 **Try this later:** Say *"What should I make for dinner tonight with chicken and rice?"* out loud — it's a fun first question.

**You'll know it worked when** you see the chat input box at the bottom and your name (or initials) at the top of the screen.

---

## Step 2 — Allow microphone access

When you first try to use voice mode, the app will ask, *"Allow ChatGPT to use the microphone?"* Tap **Allow**.

If you accidentally said no earlier, you can fix it:
- **iPhone:** Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone → ChatGPT → toggle on.
- **Android:** Settings → Apps → ChatGPT → Permissions → Microphone → Allow.

> 💬 **Check this:** Open your phone's microphone settings and confirm ChatGPT is listed as "Allowed."

**You'll know it worked when** the app stops showing a "Microphone disabled" warning when you tap the voice button.

---

## Step 3 — Pick your voice in Settings

Tap your **profile icon** at the top of the screen, then tap **Settings**. Look for the section labeled **Voice** (or **Voice & Audio**). There you'll see a list of voices to choose from — names like Breeze, Ember, Juniper, Cove, and others.

Tap each one to hear a short sample. Pick the voice that sounds most natural to you. Your choice is saved automatically.

> 💬 **Don't worry** if you can't pick right now — you can change your voice anytime from the same menu.

**You'll know it worked when** the app's spoken replies now use the voice you picked.

---

## Step 4 — Start a voice conversation

Back to the main chat screen. Look at the message box at the bottom. Right next to the send button, you'll see a **waveform icon** (or a small headphones icon). Tap it.

The screen changes to a full voice view — usually a soft, animated background. You'll hear a short chime. Just start talking as if you're chatting with a friend.

To stop, tap the **End** button (usually a red phone-style or X icon) at the bottom of the screen.

> 💬 **First phrase to try:** *"Hey ChatGPT, give me three quick dinner ideas using eggs."*

**You'll know it worked when** you see the wave animation move while you speak, then hear ChatGPT reply in the voice you chose.

---

## Step 5 — (Optional) Turn on the "Hey ChatGPT" wake word

If you want to start a voice chat without tapping anything, enable the wake word. In **Settings → Voice**, look for an option called **Hey ChatGPT** (or **Wake Word**). Toggle it on.

After that, with the app open in the background, saying *"Hey ChatGPT"* wakes it up. Then ask your question.

> 💬 **Honest note:** This feature isn't available in every region or on every account yet. If you don't see the toggle, it's not your phone — the option just isn't enabled for you right now.

**You'll know it worked when** you say *"Hey ChatGPT"* and the app responds with *"How can I help?"* without you tapping anything.

---

## Step 6 — Use it in real situations

Now the fun part. Try voice mode while doing something else:

- **Cooking:** *"Read me the next step of the recipe."*
- **Driving:** *"What's the weather like today?"* (don't look at the screen).
- **Walking:** *"Summarize the top news in AI this week."*
- **Before a meeting:** *"Help me practice a 60-second pitch for my project."*

You can interrupt ChatGPT mid-sentence by just starting to talk — it stops and listens to you.

> 💬 **Example:** *"Hey ChatGPT, give me a 30-second summary of the email I got from Sarah."* — works great if you've connected Gmail to ChatGPT.

**You'll know it worked when** you finish a task without ever touching your screen.

---

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake: Tapping the text input box instead of the waveform icon.** Fix: The voice button is the small wave or headphones icon next to the text field, not the text field itself.
- **Mistake: Microphone permission was denied earlier.** Fix: Go to your phone's privacy settings, find ChatGPT, and turn the microphone toggle on. Then restart the app.
- **Mistake: "Advanced Voice" mode is missing or grayed out.** Fix: Advanced Voice is a paid feature. You'll need a ChatGPT Plus subscription (around $20 USD/month) to use it.
- **Mistake: ChatGPT can't hear you in a noisy room.** Fix: Get closer to the phone, or use earbuds with a mic. Voice mode works best in quieter spots.
- **Mistake: The "Hey ChatGPT" wake word doesn't trigger.** Fix: Make sure the wake-word toggle is on in Settings → Voice, and the app is open in the background. If you still don't see the option, it may not be available in your region yet.

---

## What this means for you

- **If you're new to AI:** Voice mode is the friendliest way to start. You don't have to learn how to type prompts — just talk, the way you would with a friend.
- **If you're busy or on the move:** It turns idle moments (driving, walking, cooking) into useful ones, without staring at a screen.
- **If you're worried about privacy:** ChatGPT processes your voice to reply, but you can delete past voice chats anytime under Settings → Data Controls → Clear voice history.

---
